evidence:
Most negative legs are properly paired inside their own criterion, and tests/scored/functional/prompt.md states 'A positive control must come before every negative claim. If the control cannot be performed, the criterion fails rather than passing on absence of evidence.' Verified pairings in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml: cw_format_error_keeps_draft (valid format 'as the working control'), cw_error_message_and_line (valid run first), cw_promise_rejection_message_and_line (handled rejection control), cw_stop_cancels_pending_work and cw_newer_run_supersedes (delayed control marker must appear, void-attempt rule), cw_interaction_starts_fresh_budget (first button control), cw_preview_isolation (saved library entry, health address in a normal tab, localStorage set and read back, own-preview DOM and log), cw_dynamic_code_refused (harmless string/comment draft must run), cw_stale_save_refused and cw_stale_save_keeps_draft (A's accepted Save; 'If B's Save was accepted ... this criterion fails'), cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state ('If A's library never shows B's snippet, this criterion fails'), cw_replace_all_atomic, cw_find_forward_backward_wrap, cw_block_indent_undo; polish cw_undo_redo_availability ('or if the app has no visible Undo and Redo controls') and cw_unsaved_marker. 

DEFECT (one unpaired negative leg): cw_run_starts_fresh_document, tests/scored/functional/judge.toml: 'run a first draft that adds a paragraph with a distinctive first marker to the preview and sets a global variable to a distinctive value. Confirm the first marker is shown. Then run a second draft that ... writes into the preview whether that global variable is defined. The preview must now show the second marker, must not show the first marker, and must report the variable as not defined. Fails if ... the second run can see the first run's variable.' The page-content leg has its success case (first marker confirmed shown). The variable leg has none: nothing requires the first run to show, with the same probe, that the variable IS defined in the run that set it, and the criterion does not say how the variable must be set or read. The public requirement is behaviour.md line 3 'Nothing from an earlier run, neither its page content nor its variables, carries into the next one.' The scripted golden fixture happens to use 'typeof window.leftover' (qc/repairs/.../tests/runtime.cjs line 91) but the judge is free to write the fixture ('You may choose the exact fixture text'), so that choice is not guaranteed in a judge run. 

Notes, not counted as the failure: (a) cw_history_restore_retry lets the 'no fifth revision' leg be left out when the restore request cannot be recorded and replayed, and it does not require evidence that a replay actually reached the server (a replay rejected for an unrelated reason also yields no fifth revision); the first restore creating revision four is the paired success, so a dead app cannot earn the criterion, but that one leg can be earned without evidence. (b) Polish cw_controls_keyboard_and_focus counts only controls that are 'offered' and 'enabled' and says 'A control the app does not have at all is scored elsewhere, not here', with no minimum set of controls that must be reached, so an app with few or permanently disabled controls is checked against a nearly empty set. (c) tests/scored/polish/prompt.md does not carry the positive-control sentence that the functional prompt has; its two criteria with negative legs embed their own controls, so no defect follows today. 

Evidence limits: no configured judge run exists for these bytes (index scope statement); the hosted run is on an earlier candidate and the scripted golden run is not judge behaviour. No runtime measurement shows how a judge authors the fresh-document fixture.
counterexample: Weak app: JS mode runs the draft inside a module script or a wrapping function (for example an async IIFE, a common way to support top-level await and error capture), and between runs it reuses the same preview document and only empties document.body. This violates behaviour.md line 3 for variables: window-level state, timers and listeners of the earlier run survive. Judge fixture allowed by the criterion: first draft 'var cwLeft = "V1"; const p = document.createElement("p"); p.textContent = "FIRST"; document.body.append(p);', second draft appends 'SECOND ' + (typeof cwLeft). In this app cwLeft was never a global (it was scoped to the wrapper), the body was emptied, so the preview shows 'SECOND undefined' and no FIRST: every listed step holds and the criterion passes although the document is not fresh. With a control in run one (same expression reports the variable as defined) the fixture would be exposed as non-probing and the judge would have to set it on window, where this app fails.
suggested_fix: In cw_run_starts_fresh_document add the matching success case for the variable leg, in the task-specific criterion only: have the first draft set the value as a property of window and also write into the preview, with the same expression the second draft will use (for example typeof window.NAME), that it is defined; require the judge to confirm the first run reports it as defined before the second run, and add 'or if the first run did not report the variable as defined' to the fail conditions. Optionally: for cw_history_restore_retry require the judge to quote the replay's response status so a replay that never reached the app is not counted as idempotence; consider copying the positive-control sentence into the polish prompt.
